name: Andrew
overview: Andrew is a male disciple of YHVH, known primarily as the brother of Simon Peter. He was a fisherman by trade and hailed from the city of Bethsaida. Andrew was also one of the Twelve Apostles chosen by Jesus, marking him as a significant follower during Jesus' earthly ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Andrew' appears as a proper name without a specified meaning in the provided references. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God or carries a unique theological meaning within the given data.
familyAndRelationships: Andrew is explicitly identified as the brother of Simon Peter, establishing a direct family connection. He is also explicitly described as a disciple and apostle of YHVH. Additionally, there is an inferred relationship to John as a son, though this is less direct. Beyond these, Scripture does not record further family relationships for Andrew in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Andrew's significance in Scripture is highlighted by his role as one of the Twelve Apostles, chosen by Jesus to be part of His closest followers. His background as a fisherman and his origin from Bethsaida provide context to his life before discipleship. Being the brother of Simon Peter, who is a prominent apostle, further connects him to the central narrative of Jesus' ministry. Andrew's inclusion among the Twelve underscores his importance in the foundation of the early church.
